solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A lute Elvis played on screen (10)

indicatorNotes.played: the letters are played about with, like notes rearranged

annotation.surface: Elvis strums a lute in one of his films.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical picture makes 'played' look like strumming, and 'on screen' like a film setting, when it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Televisual describes what appears on a television screen.

entries.clue: Greasy head of slippery child (6)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a kiddy is a small child

annotation.surface: A slippery child is covered in grease.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slippery' sits so well beside 'Greasy' that it reads as more definition; only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a road that makes tyres skid is slick with grease or ice.

entries.clue: Genius‘s supporter getting emails here? (8)

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
the inbox is where emails arrive

annotation.surface: A genius's backer is being sent lots of emails.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. 'Supporter' suggests a patron, not underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: Brainbox is informal British for a very clever person.

entries.clue: Dog that’s mine short of tracks (6)

indicatorNotes.short of: the mine is left without the tracks

blocks.note: a colliery is a coal mine
RY = railway, a common abbreviation; these letters are removed

annotation.surface: A dog belonging to me has gone off the path.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as a possessive, not a pit. Take RY from COLLIERY.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Border and rough breeds are dogs bred for herding sheep.

entries.clue: Peerage upset with new colour (3-5)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters of peerage are knocked over and rearranged

blocks.note: N = new, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: The aristocracy is upset by a new colour, perhaps on a coat of arms.
annotation.walkthrough: The peerage is the British nobility; its seven letters plus N make the colour.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a light yellowish green like fresh peas is one colour among many.

entries.clue: Soar having clipped the first wing (4)

indicatorNotes.having clipped the first: the first letter is cut off

annotation.surface: A bird tries to soar with a clipped wing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a bird with a clipped wing, so 'wing' looks like part of the scene, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A limb can be a wing or branch of a building or organisation.

entries.clue: Wave of foam has run inside cup (7)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' places one thing within another, so R sits within the cup's letters

blocks.note: a beaker is a drinking cup
R = run, from cricket scoring; goes inside

annotation.surface: Foam from a drink spills over and runs down the cup.
annotation.walkthrough: The foam suggests a frothy drink, but it is the sea's foam.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a large wave that curls over and bursts into white foam on the shore.

entries.clue: Caress and stroke US glam rock band (9,4)

blocks.note: Kiss, the face-painted American rock band

annotation.surface: A fan caresses and strokes a member of a US glam rock band.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caress and stroke' look like two synonyms; stroke is the swimming stroke.
annotation.definitionFit: A butterfly kiss is a caress made by fluttering the eyelashes against someone's skin.

entries.clue: First chance (7)

blocks.note: first as in the first night of a show or the first move in chess
a chance or opportunity, as in a gap in the market

annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings; 'First' is adjectival as in the opening day.
annotation.definitionFit: Opening means first in order and also an opportunity.

entries.clue: Protest action for all Greeks, I learnt, misguided (7,6)

indicatorNotes.misguided: the letters are led astray into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone learns that Greek workers staged a wrong-headed mass protest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For all' is part of the definition: it is what makes the strike general.
annotation.definitionFit: A general strike is a stoppage by workers across all industries.

entries.clue: Everyday routine ending in disappointment, study works (9)

indicatorNotes.ending in: take the letter at the end

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
a mill is a factory, or works

annotation.surface: A daily grind that ends in disappointment, though studying pays off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as a verb, but it is a noun meaning a factory.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the machine you walk on without getting anywhere stands for a dull daily routine.

entries.clue: Good, a good French country (5)

annotation.surface: A French country described as good twice over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French' belongs to the wordplay, not the country: Gabon is in Africa, though French-speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: Gabon is a country in west-central Africa.

entries.clue: School closed if yard’s fenced off (5)

indicatorNotes.fenced off: the answer is penned in by the surrounding letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of closed, through if, into the start of yard's

annotation.surface: A school shuts because its yard has been fenced off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' is a verb here, meaning to teach, so the swap works: to school someone is to edify them.
annotation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct or improve someone, as to school them.

entries.clue: Shriek in alarm, perhaps? One may have hives (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the shriek goes in the alarm

blocks.note: a beeper is one kind of alarm
eek! is a shriek; goes inside

annotation.surface: Someone shrieks in alarm, then learns they have come out in hives.
annotation.walkthrough: Hives is also a skin rash, which is why shrieking in alarm seems natural; here they are beehives.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the hives are beehives, and whoever tends them has them.

entries.clue: Men’s clothing accessory, something fabricated that needs no introduction (4-3,3)

indicatorNotes.needs no introduction: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: pork pie = lie, in rhyming slang (usually shortened to porky)

annotation.surface: A fashion accessory so well known it needs no introduction.
annotation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang pairs a phrase with a word it rhymes with: pork pie, or porky, means a lie. 'Needs no introduction' sounds like praise but cuts the T from THAT.
annotation.definitionFit: A pork-pie hat is a flat-topped men's hat with a round crown.

entries.clue: Throw dummy on floor, initially (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of floor
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the dummy follows F

blocks.note: a lummox is a clumsy, stupid person

annotation.surface: Someone flings a ventriloquist's dummy to the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like a physical toss, but it means to confuse.
annotation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, which is what flummox means.

entries.clue: Poor woman OK about dismissal, finally steps back? (8)

indicatorNotes.Poor: the letters are in poor order
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of dismissal

annotation.surface: A poor woman, fine about being fired, finally backs away.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the moonwalk is a dance whose steps glide backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The moonwalk, made famous by Michael Jackson, is a dance move that seems to step forward while sliding back.

entries.clue: Party mischief maker ultimately lost power (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately lost: 'ultimately' points at the final letter and 'lost' says it goes missing

annotation.surface: A political party's troublemaker has lost power in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' seems to modify 'lost power', but it tells you to drop the last letter of TROLL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having the upper hand over something is having power over it.

entries.clue: Real company on centre ground (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, company sits on top of the rest
indicatorNotes.ground: centre is ground down and reshaped

annotation.surface: A genuine firm is occupying the political centre ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Centre ground' reads as a political phrase, but 'ground' is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Concrete means real and tangible, not abstract.

entries.clue: Shout now if ordering fish (9)

indicatorNotes.ordering: now if is put into a new order

annotation.surface: A diner shouts at a waiter to order fish right now.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' fits a restaurant, but it rearranges the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this tuna, named for its yellow fins, is one kind of fish.

entries.clue: Set off wearing cooler tie (6)

indicatorNotes.off: a plan gone off has gone wrong, so the letters of set go astray
indicatorNotes.wearing: the cooler wears the letters, holding them inside

annotation.surface: Someone sets off wearing a trendier tie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is a device, the fan, not 'more fashionable'; 'tie' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to tie a knot or a lace is to secure it.

entries.clue: Popular place for advice (5)

annotation.surface: A well-liked place to go and get advice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Place' reads as a noun here, but it is the verb put.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: opinions contributed to a project count as advice.

entries.clue: Blank design or embroidery’s framed (6)

indicatorNotes.framed: the answer is held within the frame of the surrounding words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of design, through or, into the start of embroidery's

annotation.surface: A plain design, or someone's embroidery, hangs framed on the wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blank' looks like an adjective describing the design, but it is a verb: to blank someone is to ignore them.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: to blank someone is to snub them by acting as if they are not there.

entries.clue: Relative on Sunset Boulevard, say, wife (2-3)

blocks.note: Sunset Boulevard is a street in LA, so being on it is being IN LA

annotation.surface: A relative, perhaps a wife, lives on Sunset Boulevard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Sunset Boulevard as an example of somewhere in LA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's mother.

entries.clue: O sugar! (4)

blocks.note: O is shaped like a zero, and nil in tennis scoring has its own word
sugar is a term of endearment, like darling

annotation.surface: A mild curse: O sugar!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sugar!' reads as a polite swear word; it is a pet name, like love.
annotation.definitionFit: Love means nil in tennis, and is a term of endearment like sugar.

entries.clue: See the setter by mostly calm wildlife sanctuary (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: to get a point is to see it
the setter refers to themself as I

annotation.surface: A visitor is told to see the setter beside a quiet nature reserve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' suggests visiting, but it means understand, as in 'I get it'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a national park in Tanzania famous for its wildlife.

entries.clue: Spanish article is back in Spanish city (7)

indicatorNotes.back: the whole run of letters goes backwards

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist

annotation.surface: A Spanish news article has returned to a Spanish city.
annotation.walkthrough: ELLIVES turned around gives SEVILLE. 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Andalusian capital, home of flamenco, is one city in Spain.

entries.clue: About right, a treat roughly chopped and served raw (7)

indicatorNotes.roughly: the letters are arranged only roughly

annotation.surface: A kitchen treat is roughly chopped and served raw, about right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition, which describes steak tartare.
annotation.definitionFit: Tartare describes meat or fish finely chopped and served raw.
